problems.summary: The wall-clock dispatch bound killed Bob's 1DMIX-049 implementation turn after its rebuild, rerun, capture and test-writing work was already durable on disk, discarding only the sealed report and forcing a whole extra followup dispatch to re-narrate completed work.
problems.evidence: dispatch_log.jsonl: 12 events with error=='timeout' out of 115 bob/richard role dispatches (10.4%) across 10 distinct issues (1DMIX-026/032/034/039/041/042/043/048/049/050). This iteration's own event a173627c4cb841f488d3ea177051a7aa: duration_seconds 2400.04, returncode 143 (SIGTERM), report sha256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 (the digest of zero bytes). closed_issues.md:1407 records that no rebuild or measurement was redone on recovery.

problems.summary: This issue's own filed text asserted 8760 timesteps and hours of wall clock for the global_oce_latlon rerun. That figure belongs to lab_sea/1DMIX-026; the real count is 720 and the real run+parse cost about 14 minutes, so the issue was scoped around a hedge more expensive than the work it hedged against.
problems.evidence: closed_issues.md:1391 records the correction and the measurement: 720x43,200s = 360 days = one externForcingCycle; full Docker run 6m52s, reparse of the 13.82 GB output.txt 6m57s, against a written expectation of hours. Richard independently reconfirmed by reading both closed issues and grepping the experiment's live data file rather than accepting the narrative (closed_issues.md:1401).

solutions.reason: Diagnosis first: measure whether a progress-aware bound is achievable before touching the wall-clock bound, which exists to cap genuinely runaway spend and must keep its default.
Requires a documented sourcing rule in issue_priority.md plus a survey of the current open root ledger, neither of which belongs inside a scientific iteration.

carry_forward: Before deferring work on cost grounds, measure a cheap prefix of the real command; a figure transferred from a neighbouring experiment's record is not a measurement.
Treat a timed-out dispatch as work-of-unknown-completeness: inspect the tree before re-dispatching, and resume with followup rather than restarting.
